cohort.warning: The cohort was selected for Ordivon relevance rather than sampled randomly from all agent research. Recurrence is evidence of cross-domain convergence, not an unbiased population-frequency estimate.

hypothesisUnderTest: Robust successful structures converge toward a small recurring set of causal invariants, while failed implementations exhibit high surface diversity.
strongerRejectedForm: Failure causes are completely chaotic or structureless.

codingMethod.successUnit: unique research-group × normalized successful structural motif
codingMethod.failureUnit: unique research-group × normalized causal failure anti-law
codingMethod.normalizationBoundary: Motifs/anti-laws are Ordivon research shorthand and never owner/product authority.
codingMethod.independenceBoundary: Multiple benchmarks from one paper or follow-up lineage do not create independent research-group support.

descriptiveEntropy.interpretation: Normalized success assignments are only slightly more concentrated than normalized failure-cause assignments. This does not support a strong entropy theorem. The stronger signal is cross-domain recurrence breadth of several successful motifs, while failure manifestations remain much more heterogeneous at the source-native mechanism level.

stronglyRecurringSuccessMotifs.claim: Improvement must survive held-out/OOD/variant tests beyond the optimized signal.
Model report, textual description, public metric, memory entry or predicted state must not be collapsed into realized/verified reality.
Evaluator/verification integrity is part of the system and requires hidden/independent/anchored/state-grounded checks rather than assumed truth.
Search/harness/tool/reasoning policy should depend on task/evidence/world conditions; one fixed global operator is rarely justified.
Current task score is insufficient for recursive improvement; measure whether the system improves future improvement ability or survives further adaptation.
Adaptive orchestration/search/defense must justify its own compute/latency/complexity overhead against a strong simpler baseline.
Persistent task/improvement/memory state should retain verified causal state outside raw growing transcript.
Evidence/state needs causal/provenance/applicability binding rather than identity-free accumulation.

recurringFailureAntiLaws.claim: Optimizing a visible scalar/proxy as if it were reality invites leakage, evaluator gaming, attribution error or metric collapse.
Local benchmark/seed/literature improvement is not evidence of broader frontier/generalization progress.
Current performance does not imply descendant/metaproductive/improvement value.
Raw growing context wastes budget, while unconstrained lossy compaction can erase decisive state/constraints.
A fixed search/harness/meta policy can become the wrong operator as task/evidence conditions change.
More elaborate search/orchestration can consume more resources or complexity without causal improvement.
One domain score can collapse distinct truths such as return source, game improvement dynamics or visual/function quality.

crossPaperManifestations: prompt self-critique that accepts its own wrong answer
privilege escalation after transient tool failure
research ideation collapsing toward seed literature
unreliable world-model foresight injected into planning
meta-agent ground-truth exfiltration under optimization pressure
surfaceFailureDiversityEvidence.interpretation: Wrong implementations have many surface mechanisms. However, normalization repeatedly maps them to a smaller set of causal anti-laws; therefore the 'wrong is completely chaotic' hypothesis is rejected at the causal level.

worldModelUpdate.refinedClaim: Across independent agent-research domains, useful surviving designs repeatedly rediscover a low-dimensional set of semantic distinctions. Failed mechanisms are high-diversity in implementation and symptom, but their causal errors also recur as a smaller set of anti-laws. The research advantage comes from learning both stable positive invariants and stable negative priors, then testing them against owner reality rather than treating either as universal rules.
doNotInfer: that every successful system must share one code architecture
that all errors are predictable from a fixed taxonomy
that a normalized motif should become an Agent-facing classifier or shared service
that literature agreement outranks owner-native evidence

nextFalsifiers: Prospectively code new papers before reading their result sections and test whether the same motifs/anti-laws predict surviving versus rejected mechanisms better than chance/simple baselines.

Use materially different non-agent fields or older systems literature as an out-of-domain holdout; if the claimed stable structures disappear, convergence is field-fashion rather than deeper structure.
Track future independent replications/rebuttals of the 2026 preprints; downgrade motifs whose support vanishes when evaluators/tasks change.
Test whether anti-laws improve real frontier selection in shadow ResearchBets without recreating TM1 meta-prose overhead.
